raw_response:
I farm only 4.1 mu, so every bag of fertilizer matters. I do not like to gamble with yield. What I usually do is start from what worked the year before, then change a little if prices or weather look different. Here in Quzhou, wheat after autumn sowing and maize after wheat harvest is the normal road, so I will stay with that. I finished many years on this same pattern, and with well water in hand I can push the crop a bit and not be too afraid of dry spells. I have only two people in the house, so I will keep the work simple and use rotary tillage because it is faster and cheaper than deep ploughing every season.

For wheat, I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because I have seen cleaner stand and better ears from improved varieties in nearby fields. I will not cut fertilizer too hard on wheat, because if wheat is weak before winter and at jointing, the harvest suffers right away. I will put most of the phosphorus at sowing, some nitrogen at sowing, then topdress nitrogen with irrigation in spring. Potash I will use, but not too heavy, because on my small land I must leave money for herbicide and one or two sprays if disease shows. With well irrigation, I will usually water about 3 times for wheat: once after sowing if the ground is dry, once at jointing, and once at filling if needed.

For maize, I will use hybrid seed. Around here, good hybrid maize is worth the money. I will feed maize a little heavier than wheat on nitrogen because maize eats fertilizer fast in summer, and I do not want pale leaves when it starts stretching. I will place phosphorus and potash mostly before or at sowing, then chase nitrogen once around the big bell-mouth stage, and if the stand looks hungry I will add a little more with water. Summer rain helps, but rain is never something I trust fully, so with the well I will plan on about 2 irrigations and give more only if the weather turns dry. Pesticide I will keep to what is needed: one herbicide pass, then one or two insect or disease sprays depending on what I see. If the season is normal, I will aim for steady yield instead of trying fancy methods.
